name: app.R
content: # ===================================================================== # Rapa Nui coral spatial pattern — Pocillopora colony dispersion # Shinylive (runs entirely in the browser via WebR — no install, no server) # Proof-of-concept for SCCS-NY 2026 hands-on workshop. # Data: pre-extracted, size-filtered colony centroids (x, y in metres) # from manual segmentation of large-area-imaging orthomosaics. # Three reef sites along a wave-exposure gradient (Herlan et al., ch.2). # ===================================================================== library(shiny) library(spatstat.geom) library(spatstat.explore) # --- Sites (wave-exposure gradient) ---------------------------------- sites <- c( "Anakena — sheltered (north)" = "ana.csv", "Manavai — moderate (west)" = "man.csv", "Vaihu — exposed (southeast)" = "vhu.csv" ) # All plots are 10 m (x) x 25 m (y) = 250 m^2 WIN <- owin(xrange = c(0, 10), yrange = c(0, 25)) AREA <- 250 site_label <- function(file) names(sites)[match(file, sites)] # --- UI -------------------------------------------------------------- ui <- fluidPage( tags$head(tags$style(HTML( ".well{background:#f4f8f5} h4{color:#1b5e3f;margin-top:0}"))), titlePanel("Rapa Nui coral spatial pattern — Pocillopora dispersion"), helpText("From photos to spatial pattern: each point is a coral colony extracted", "from a segmented large-area-imaging orthomosaic. Pick a site, then ask:", "are the colonies clustered, random, or over-dispersed — and how does that", "change along the wave-exposure gradient?"), sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( selectInput("site", "Reef site (wave-exposure gradient)", choices = sites), tags$hr(), h4("Quadrat CSR test"), sliderInput("nx", "Quadrats across plot width (x)", 2, 10, 4), sliderInput("ny", "Quadrats down plot length (y)", 2, 20, 10), tags$hr(), h4("Distance function + CSR envelope"), radioButtons("fun", "Function", c("L-function L(r)" = "L", "Pair correlation g(r)" = "pcf")), sliderInput("rmax", "Max distance r (m)", 0.5, 5, 2.5, step = 0.5), sliderInput("nsim", "CSR simulations (envelope)", 0, 199, 39, step = 10), conditionalPanel( "input.site == 'vhu.csv'", checkboxInput("sub", "Subsample Vaihu to 800 colonies (speeds up envelopes)", TRUE)), actionButton("go", "Run distance function", class = "btn-primary"), helpText("Summary stats update instantly; the envelope runs when you click.") ), mainPanel( tabsetPanel( tabPanel("Point map", plotOutput("map", height = "620px")), tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary")), tabPanel("Distance function", plotOutput("envplot", height = "500px"), uiOutput("envnote")) ) ) ) ) # --- Server ---------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output, session) { # full point pattern for the selected site pp <- reactive({ df <- read.csv(input$site) ppp(df$x, df$y, window = WIN) }) # pattern used for the (heavier) envelope — optionally subsampled for Vaihu ppUse <- reactive({ X <- pp() if (isTRUE(input$sub) && input$site == "vhu.csv" && npoints(X) > 800) { set.seed(42) X <- X[sample(npoints(X), 800)] } X }) output$map <- renderPlot({ X <- pp() plot(X, main = paste0(site_label(input$site), " (n = ", npoints(X), ")"), pch = 19, cex = 0.45, cols = "#1b7837") axis(1); axis(2) title(xlab = "x (m)", ylab = "y (m)") }) output$summary <- renderPrint({ X <- pp() lam <- intensity(X) ce <- clarkevans(X)[["naive"]] cet <- clarkevans.test(X, alternative = "two.sided", nsim = 99) qt <- quadrat.test(X, nx = input$nx, ny = input$ny) nnd <- nndist(X) verdict <- if (ce < 1) "CLUSTERED (aggregated)" else if (ce > 1) "REGULAR (over-dispersed)" else "RANDOM" cat("Site: ", site_label(input$site), "\n") cat("Colonies: ", npoints(X), "\n") cat("Plot: 10 x 25 m (250 m^2)\n") cat(sprintf("Intensity: %.3f colonies / m^2\n", lam)) cat(sprintf("Mean nearest-neighbour distance: %.3f m\n\n", mean(nnd))) cat("-- Clark-Evans aggregation index --\n") cat(sprintf(" R = %.3f -> %s\n", ce, verdict)) cat(sprintf(" test p-value (two-sided, 99 sims) = %.4g\n\n", cet$p.value)) cat(sprintf("-- Quadrat chi-square test of CSR (%d x %d grid) --\n", input$nx, input$ny)) cat(sprintf(" chi-sq = %.1f, p-value = %.4g\n", qt$statistic, qt$p.value)) cat(" (small p = significant departure from complete spatial randomness)\n") }) # envelope computed only when the button is pressed env <- eventReactive(input$go, { X <- ppUse() rr <- seq(0, input$rmax, length.out = 200) fun <- if (input$fun == "L") Lest else pcf if (input$nsim > 0) { envelope(X, fun, nsim = input$nsim, r = rr, verbose = FALSE) } else { fun(X, r = rr) } }) output$envplot <- renderPlot({ e <- env() ttl <- if (input$fun == "L") "L-function with CSR envelope" else "Pair correlation g(r) with CSR envelope" plot(e, main = ttl, legend = TRUE) }) output$envnote <- renderUI({ req(input$go) if (input$fun == "L") { helpText(HTML(paste0( "How to read it: the dashed line is the CSR expectation. ", "Observed above the grey envelope = clustering at that ", "distance; below = over-dispersion; inside = consistent ", "with random. The envelope is the range of ", input$nsim, " simulated random patterns."))) } else { helpText(HTML(paste0( "How to read it: g(r) = 1 under complete spatial randomness. ", "g(r) > 1 = more colony pairs at distance r than random ", "(clustering); < 1 = fewer (inhibition). ", "Grey band = ", input$nsim, " CSR simulations."))) } }) } shinyApp(ui, server)

name: README.md
content:
# Rapa Nui coral spatial pattern — local R app

A small Shiny app that runs your Chapter 2 spatial-pattern analysis on the
pre-extracted *Pocillopora* colony centroids for the three reef sites
(Anakena, Manavai, Vaihu). It's the same `app.R` we'll later compile to a
browser (Shinylive) build for the workshop — this folder is for running and
testing it on your own computer.

## What it does

Pick a site, and the app builds a `spatstat` point pattern (10 × 25 m plot)
and reports:

- colony count and intensity (colonies / m²), mean nearest-neighbour distance
- **Clark-Evans** aggregation index + test (clustered / random / over-dispersed)
- **quadrat χ² test** of complete spatial randomness (CSR)
- **L-function** or **pair-correlation g(r)** with a CSR simulation envelope

The three sites already show the gradient from your dissertation: Anakena
(sheltered) R ≈ 0.80 and Manavai (moderate) R ≈ 0.60 are **clustered**, while
Vaihu (exposed) R ≈ 1.26 is **over-dispersed**.

## Data

`ana.csv`, `man.csv`, `vhu.csv` — the `*_poci_sizefiltered.csv` centroid files
(columns `x`, `y` in metres), copied from
`R Final/output_dispersion/` in your Chapter 2 folder.

## How to run (local)

1. Install the packages once (in R or RStudio):

   ```r
   install.packages(c("shiny", "spatstat.geom", "spatstat.explore"))
   ```

2. Run the app, pointing at this folder:

   ```r
   shiny::runApp("path/to/this/folder")
   ```

   In RStudio you can also just open `app.R` and click **Run App**.

## How to build the browser (Shinylive) version

From the folder that CONTAINS this folder:

```r
install.packages("shinylive")              # once
shinylive::export("rpn-spatial-local", "site")
httpuv::runStaticServer("site")            # test locally in your browser
```

Then push the contents of `site/` to a GitHub repo (add an empty `.nojekyll`
file first) and enable GitHub Pages.

## Notes

- These CSVs have only `x, y` (no colony area), so the app reports colony
  *intensity/density*, not percent cover.
- To add the live-vs-dead **Lcross** bivariate analysis, add the matching
  dead-colony centroid files.
